      <title>Hilarious quips and ‘100,000-volt’ energy: the hypemen (and women) redefining Afrobeats music</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/18/lagos-hypemen-redefining-afrobeats-music-afrohype</link>
      <description><p>Style of emceeing based on high-octane, ad-libbed vocals has flourished thanks to its unique way of captivating crowds</p><p>For the 2015 freshmen cohort of the history degree programme at the University of Lagos, their classmate’s first-semester presentation was so captivating that they began calling him Toby Shang, after the 16th-century Chinese dynasty he had focused on.</p><p>His crowd engagement that day had been harnessed from his high school days as a ginger-man (energiser) in a three-man band and as a private tutor. By his final year at university, his viral catchphrases and infectious energy had resulted in a hit song, Shedibalabala. Today, he is one of the self-acclaimed “evangelists and pioneers” in the Afrobeats sub-genre some are now calling Afrohype or lamba.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/18/lagos-hypemen-redefining-afrobeats-music-afrohype">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Health minister says government ‘did not authorize’ Danish-led hepatitis B trial in babies backed by RFK Jr</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/guinea-bissau">Guinea-Bissau</a> has not approved the controversial <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/hepatitis-b">hepatitis B</a> study in newborns that would be funded by the US government and private partners, the African country’s minister of health said on Tuesday.</p><p>The study, which would not investigate the safety or effectiveness of vaccines but would instead track “nonspecific” health outcomes like overall mortality or neurodevelopmental conditions, has been championed by Robert F Kennedy Jr, secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime anti-vaccine activist.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/14/guinea-bissau-vaccine-hepatitis-b-trial-denial">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Hurricane Trudy menaces Mexico’s Pacific coast and Greece hit by deadly floods</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/oct/19/hurricane-trudy-mexico-pacific-coast-greece-floods</link>
      <description><p>Trudy weakens to tropical storm after warnings of strong winds and heavy rain, while one person killed in Greece</p><p>In contrast to the quiet Atlantic hurricane season, there has been ongoing activity in the Pacific, with Trudy being the 22nd and latest named system. The <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/17/hurricane-trudy-mexico">category 2 hurricane</a> remained roughly 100 miles (160km) south-west of the coast of Mexico, meaning the worst of the conditions stayed offshore. However, the US National Hurricane Center put coastal parts of the states of Jalisco, Michoacán and Colima under hurricane warnings, with sustained winds of up to 60-90mph forecast on Sunday.</p><p>Rainfall totals of 100-150mm were likely for these areas, prompting warnings of flooding and landslides. Warnings also covered the risk of a dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves in areas of onshore winds across the coast of south-western Mexico. By Monday morning, Trudy had weakened and been downgraded to a tropical storm, with coastal warnings being lifted.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/oct/19/hurricane-trudy-mexico-pacific-coast-greece-floods">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>In today’s newsletter: Violent riots and looting have dominated the headlines, but the unrest gripping the country and beyond reflects deeper public anger over everyday issues</p><p></p><p>Good morning. I bet your weekend was better than Emmanuel Macron’s. On Friday, the evening before mass protests that were planned across France,<strong> </strong>he attended a Céline Dion concert in Paris with his wife, Brigitte, prompting comparisons to Louis XIV and Marie Antoinette. On Sunday evening, he was forced to give a televised speech <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/18/french-government-crisis-talks-violent-unrest-policing-macron">condemning the</a> “unbridled violence” and riots that erupted in French cities over the weekend.</p><p>The rioters that burned makeshift barricades of bicycles in Paris, destroyed the steeple of Limoges’ town hall and set fire to Lyon’s tourism office were described as “LE CHAOS” on the front page of La Tribune Dimanche, and “SCENES D’INSURRECTION” on Le Parisien Dimanche. By Sunday, protests had also taken place<strong> </strong>in Spain, Portugal and Italy.</p><p><em><strong>The Vatican</strong></em> | Pope Leo <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/18/pope-leo-resume-activities-removal-lung-cancer-tumour">told a crowd</a> gathered in St Peter’s Square on Sunday that he would “gradually resume” his activities, at his first appearance before the faithful since undergoing an operation to remove a cancerous tumour from his lung.</p><p><em><strong>UK news</strong></em> | A “well-known individual” <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/oct/16/well-known-individual-tries-to-secure-permanent-injunction-against-guardian-and-itn">is trying to secure</a> a permanent injunction against the Guardian and ITN to prevent them from publishing details of serious allegations made against him.</p><p><em><strong>US politics</strong></em> | Donald Trump fired his immediately embattled new press secretary, Katie Zacharia, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/16/katie-zacharia-fired-press-secretary">on Friday evening</a> after just five days in the job. The conservative commentator becomes the shortest serving occupant of the role in US history.</p><p><em><strong>Reform</strong></em> | A Reform UK mayor is under police investigation for allegedly showing “naked and sexualised” images of himself to a female member of staff. Luke Campbell, a former Olympic boxing champion, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/oct/18/police-investigate-reform-mayor-allegedly-sharing-naked-sexualised-images-of-himself">is understood</a> to have been questioned under caution by Humberside police.</p><p><em><strong>Energy</strong></em> | The development of a huge AI datacentre hailed by the UK government <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/oct/18/microsoft-drops-huge-ai-datacentre-project-in-essex-over-power-supply-concerns">has received a fresh setback</a> after Microsoft pulled out of the project over concerns about power supplies.</p><p><em><strong>Monday</strong></em> | The two-week biodiversity summit, Cop17, begins in Yerevan, Armenia, as countries come together to seek to protect nature.</p><p><em><strong>Tuesday</strong></em> | The Covid-19 inquiry publishes its report on the adult social care sector.</p><p><em><strong>Sunday</strong></em> | Incumbent Lula da Silva takes on Flavio Bolsonaro in the run-off of the Brazil general election.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/monday-briefing-what-you-need-to-know-about-a-weekend-of-chaos-in-france">Continue reading...</a></description>
